To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) a hierarchical architecture for intelligent controllers is needed to achieve the necessary reliability, and (2) the architecture should be based on a modular design with distributed autonomy.

the proposed architecture for hierarchical systems is capable of satisfying the stringent requirements for reliability and validation that are imposed on nuclear safety systems, and that the proposed architecture can be implemented incrementally, thus facilitating the transition to intelligent systems.

the use of intelligent controllers for safety systems of nuclear power plants is feasible if the control architecture is designed to be modular and if the controllers are designed to be distributed autonomous.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of intelligent controllers for nuclear power plants, and with the development of a system architecture that will facilitate their implementation and testing.
the development of intelligent controllers that are suitable for use in safety systems of nuclear power plants.
a methodology for developing and testing control systems that can be implemented in complex, real-time, dynamic environments such as nuclear power plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of intelligent controllers in safety systems of nuclear power plants is not acceptable.
the proposed architecture is not a panacea for all the problems of nuclear power plant control.
the use of intelligent controllers in nuclear power plants is not yet practical and will not become so until a more complete and convincing validation methodology has been developed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concept of intelligent control is compatible with the stringent requirements for reliability, safety and validation in the nuclear power generation industry.
the proposed architecture is compatible with current requirements for nuclear power plants.
it is possible to develop intelligent controllers that are acceptable in the nuclear industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear power industry has the capability to develop and use intelligent control systems.
it is possible to develop a control architecture that is both intelligent and reliable.
intelligent systems can be designed to be robust, verifiable, and reliable, and can thus be acceptable for use in safety systems in the nuclear power plant industry.
